candidates.tagline: 40 parking spots saved. Bike lane built. It ends at stairs.
candidates.story: NYC DOT installed a protected bike lane on Riverside Drive in Inwood that funnels cyclists to a flight of stairs with no bike runnel, because the community board vetoed the simpler route to preserve 40 parking spaces — so cyclists carry their bikes up the stairs or skip the new lane entirely.
candidates.why_funny: The official answer to 'we can't lose 40 parking spots' was a fully engineered protected bike lane that still requires cyclists to hump their bikes up a flight of stairs — which they don't, so the shiny new lane sits empty.
candidates.alt: Cyclist hauling a bicycle up a flight of concrete stairs beneath the Henry Hudson Parkway overpass to access the Hudson River Greenway, with the new empty protected bike lane visible below

candidates.tagline: $249. Always listening. Forgets you in 30 days. Meet Friend 2.0.
candidates.story: Friend launched its AI pendant 2.0 in July 2026 at double the original price ($249 vs $129), now with a built-in speaker so it can talk back — but without a $10/month subscription, the device deletes all its memories of you every 30 days, meaning your AI bestie has to re-learn who you are from scratch each month.
candidates.why_funny: A device marketed as a cure for loneliness charges you double to listen to everything you say, then ghosts your entire relationship history unless you keep paying — the AI companion that forgets you is now louder and more expensive.
candidates.alt: Person wearing a small white circular Friend AI pendant around their neck while brushing their teeth, with the always-on microphone recording their morning routine
